headline: The School Committee reviewed a preliminary 5.36% budget increase and Neary renovation designs, while library trustees prepared for upcoming construction grants.
synopsis: The Southborough School Committee examined a preliminary FY28 operating budget of $27.5 million, a 5.36% increase driven largely by salaries, transportation, and special education tuition. Committee members also weighed the trade-offs of seeking state funding versus town financing for the proposed Neary Elementary renovation, even as the Neary roof replacement wrapped up roughly $1.6 million under budget. Meanwhile, the Library Board of Trustees verified compliance with state materials spending standards and voted to solicit proposals for a building condition assessment ahead of an upcoming state grant round.

highlights.title: Preliminary FY28 school operating budget projects 5.36% increase
highlights.why: School administrators presented a $27,514,571 budget proposal for FY28, showing an increase of $1,399,853 driven by rising salaries, special education tuition, and transportation. Meeting the town's recommended 3% growth target would require over $616,000 in reductions.

highlights.title: Neary renovation designs presented amid debate over state partnership
highlights.why: Architects shared refined schematic designs to renovate Neary Elementary, add a full gymnasium, and remove modular classrooms. Officials debated whether partnering with the state school building program could push completion to 2035 and see cost savings erased by construction inflation.

highlights.title: Neary roof replacement nears completion $1.6 million under budget
highlights.why: The Neary roof project reached over 97% completion with projected final costs of $2.91 million against a $4.5 million appropriation. Unused borrowing authorization will help reduce the town's overall debt service burden.

highlights.title: Library initiates building condition assessment for state grant round
highlights.why: Trustees authorized the library director to seek proposals under $10,000 for a comprehensive building assessment. The study and an upcoming community survey will support an application to the Massachusetts Public Library Construction Program.

highlights.title: Library trustees advance formal patron behavior and trespass policy
highlights.why: Following an Election Day incident and police inquiries regarding library trespass authority, trustees directed staff to draft a formal patron code of conduct and trespass policy for review with legal counsel.
